correctness.rationale: For distinct letters b,a, the scattered pair ba is absent precisely when last(a)<first(b); this recovers an interval order P. The pair aa is absent exactly for singleton letters S. These point intervals must be pairwise comparable (independent in incomparability graph), and each has a clique neighborhood (simplicial). Conversely, a robust strict-overlap interval representation exists for any finite interval order. Each simplicial interval and its incomparable neighbors have a common open Helly intersection, permitting contraction to a point; independent marked intervals are pairwise disjoint, so all contractions commute. Reading endpoints yields the exact prescribed two-subsequence spectrum. The lower bound 2q-|S| follows from required multiplicities and is attained. Adjacent simplicial vertices are true twins, implying a disjoint union of simplicial cliques and the product-sum generating function. The supplied clean standalone checker implements two separate finite enumerations through q=5 and passed; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural level-two subsequence-realizability problem asks which absence/presence patterns of pairs and repeated pairs can arise from a single word and what the shortest realizing length is. The theorem settles both for all finite alphabet sizes using a structural interval-order-plus-simplicial criterion and gives the complete minimum-length distribution as a meaningful exact combinatorial sum. The Helly contraction and true-twin graph decomposition expose a nontrivial bridge between formal-language congruence classes and interval geometry, not a routine numerical increment. No claim of new algorithms or the already known totals is made.
